chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman, from Mis'mam, Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "There is no manumission except after ownership."

key_terms.عِتْق: Manumission or freeing of a slave

ai.seo_question: What is the primary condition for valid manumission of a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Sahih al-Tusi establishes the prerequisite of actual ownership (milkiyyah) for valid manumission, ensuring that a master cannot free a slave he does not legally possess. It serves as a foundational principle in Shia fiqh to prevent disputes over property rights and clarifies that the act of freeing is a disposition of one's own property, thereby requiring clear title before the transaction is legally binding.
